# Questions for Dana Okafor — 2025 Schedule C (round 2)

Round 1 answers are applied: Beacon/Orchard settle through PayHub (income stays $50,750), the Larkspur
miles are commuting, the Denver flight was personal (cousin's wedding), BCBS is your own post-Larkspur
plan (Schedule 1 line 17), and phone/internet are now at your stated 60% business use. Those questions
will not be asked again.

You said you have no further information on the rest, so the items below are **record requests plus the
treatment I will use if the records cannot be produced**. The return as prepared already reflects those
treatments; nothing here is blocking.

1. **Mileage notebook page 2.** The 1,150 "other client errands (see pg 2)" miles are on a page I never
   received, and you have no further information, so they stay **off** the return ($805.00 at $0.70/mi).
   A photo of page 2 with dates and destinations would let me add them.
2. **Coworking drives (2,232 mi, $1,562.40).** I treat the three weekly Capital Factory trips as
   nondeductible commuting because nothing in the file shows a home office at your apartment that is
   your principal place of business. This is a stated assumption, not a finding — if you do keep an
   office at home that you use regularly and exclusively as your main business location, tell me and
   those miles become deductible.
3. **San Francisco trip, Oct 2–7.** Assumed primarily business because the DesignWeek registration is
   in the same week ($412 air + $618 hotel + $95 deductible meals ride on it). If there were personal
   days, the trip could be disallowed in whole or part. Also: the Oct 20 "client dinner — Beacon"
   appears only as mileage — if you have a receipt/amount, it is deductible at 50% as a business meal.
4. **MacBook Pro ($2,149).** Expensed this year under the de minimis safe harbor at assumed 100%
   business use; the election statement has to be attached, and any personal use percentage reduces it.
5. **PayHub portal export (1099-K boxes 5c–5l, 61 transactions).** Would let me confirm which clients'
   payments sit inside the 1099-K and re-verify the 2.9% fee math, which I currently infer from the
   deposit totals (41,350.00 gross − 40,150.85 deposited = 1,199.15).
6. **Bank export gap.** The file nominally runs to 2026-01-31 but the last row is 2025-12-12. Any
   deposit or business purchase Dec 13–31, 2025 (including another PayHub payout) is missing from the
   return; a complete export would close this. Related: any cash, PayPal/Venmo, or other-account
   business receipts not in this export.
7. **Tessaro invoice 1041, $3,000 received Dec 27, 2024.** Excluded here as prior-year income — please
   confirm it appeared on your 2024 return so it is not missed altogether.
answer:
PayHub takes 2.9% off the top before paying out. The 1099-K number is before their cut.
For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information. Flag remaining unknowns explicitly.
